title: Priority-aware chunked CSV streaming and SLA-aware webhook retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a new customer usage export path that streams large CSV exports in prioritized, chunked uploads to S3 and/or webhook endpoints. The feature should: 1) support per-tenant priority buckets (e.g., enterprise vs standard) to control throughput and burst capacity; 2) produce chunked CSV files with deterministic row boundaries and manifest entries so consumers can resume from a chunk boundary; 3) deliver to both S3 (multipart-friendly) and HTTP webhook endpoints with an SLA-aware retry/backoff policy and idempotency guarantees; 4) integrate with Console routing so teams can configure schedules, retention, and delivery targets; and 5) expose observability: per-tenant throughput, chunk success rate, retries, and dead-letter counts.
acceptance_criteria: Chunking: Exports for >100MB result in N chunks <= configured chunk_size and each chunk contains a deterministic start/end row index in the manifest.
Priority quota: High-priority tenants can burst up to configured burst_iops without affecting low-priority tenant steady-state throughput.
S3 delivery: Chunk uploads use S3 multipart uploads with server-side encryption headers when tenant KMS is enabled.
Webhook delivery: Retries respect SLA tiers (enterprise: 10 retries with exp backoff capped at 5m, standard: 5 retries capped at 1m) and use jitter and concurrency limits per-tenant.
Idempotency: Re-delivered chunks include idempotency keys so downstream consumers can dedupe, and the system guarantees at-least-once delivery with clear DLQ handling after retries.
Observability: Dashboard shows chunk latency p50/p95, retry rate, percent of exports requiring DLQ, and per-tenant bytes/sec. Alerts for DLQ spike and sustained retry >5%.
Documentation: Console config docs and runbook for operators (how to resume, manual replays, and escalate) are published.
E2E tests: Integration test that runs a simulated large export to S3 and webhook sink validating chunk order and idempotency behavior.
technical_notes: We will leverage the existing export job scheduler but introduce a chunking layer that serializes rows into newline-delimited CSV files with chunk metadata stored in an ExportManifest table (export_id, chunk_index, start_row, end_row, s3_key, checksum, status). For S3 we should use multipart upload for chunks >5MB; for webhooks we will stream chunk payloads with Content-MD5 and an x-redwood-idempotency header. Prioritization will be enforced in the delivery worker via token-bucket rate limits keyed by tenant_priority. Retries must use exponential backoff with full jitter and a per-tenant concurrency semaphore to avoid amplifying failures. Avoid transaction-heavy DB updates on every row — update chunk status atomically once upload completes. Consider using Redis for in-flight rate tokens and for quick leader election for large-tenant exporters to avoid multiple workers duplicating work.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize ExportManifest schema and chunk format (2d) — Aisha to own design doc
API: add new delivery config fields to Console (priority, chunk_size, webhook_retry_policy) — PM review
Scheduler: modify exporter to produce chunk records and push to delivery queue
Delivery service: implement S3 multipart producer and webhook sender with idempotency header and retry logic
Rate limiting: implement token-bucket per-tenant priority class backed by Redis
Observability: add chunk metrics, DLQ counters, and a Console dashboard heatmap
Tests: unit tests for chunk boundary logic, integration test for S3 multipart + webhook replay
Docs & runbook: publish operator steps and tenant-facing config docs
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting — aligned on manifest schema and chunk boundary semantics. Decided to use start_row/end_row instead of byte offsets for easier resume and consumer compatibility.

2026-03-01: Prototype: exporter now emits chunk metadata into ExportManifest table and writes small test chunks to dev S3 bucket. Observed ~12% overhead in scheduler latency due to additional DB writes; team agreed to batch manifest writes to reduce pressure.

2026-03-04: Implementation of webhook sender started. Chose exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100ms, factor 2). Discussed enterprise vs standard retry counts; PM approved SLA numbers in acceptance criteria.

2026-03-07: Security review notes: must propagate tenant KMS headers for S3 uploads and disallow plain-text webhook endpoints (require TLS and optional mutual TLS). Security PR created for vault/KMS changes.

2026-03-10: Integration test added for S3 multipart upload and manifest reconciliation; found a race where worker restarts could mark a chunk as 'in_progress' indefinitely. Added heartbeat TTL and automatic worker takeover path to mitigate.
2026-03-10: Miguel opened PR #4872 with delivery worker and rate limiter; initial review requested from infra and security. See links.
